<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to determine which statement is incorrect.

We review each statement:

A. "Even under extreme noise conditions, SDDPM still can recover most of the high frequency information of the original picture". In the paper, they claim that SDDPM performs well even under worst noise, and retains high frequency details. Yes, correct.

B. "The denoising ability of the baseline convolution structure decreases exponentially with the increase of noise". Are they saying baseline conv models (DnCNN, SCU, SwinIR) degrade exponentially? In the paper, they say performance of DnCNN, SCU, SwinIR is not exponential? They mention that performance for DnCNN, SCU, SwinIR vary erratic but not linear. They say "the PSNR and SSIM scores for most of the baseline models are much lower than the proposed model in all cases. In some cases (DnCNN and SCU), the PSNR scores are somewhat erratic. In these cases, the usual trend is not observed, and the performance metrics vary arbitrarily within a small interval." So they didn't claim exponential. The exponential claim is not supported. So statement (B) likely incorrect.

C. "SwinIR's structure contains 3 convolutional layers and a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB)". The paper says: "SwinIR's structure contains three phases: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and image reconstruction. The shallow features are extracted by a convolutional layer whereas the deep features are extracted by a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB) followed by a final convolutional layer." So they mention convolutional layer, then RSTB, then final convolution. But they didn't say 3 convolutional layers. Is there 3 convolutional layers? Let's check: The architecture might have a single conv layer for shallow features, then RSTB, then final conv. So not 3 conv layers. So statement C is likely incorrect. However, the statement says "SwinIR's structure contains 3 convolutional layers AND a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB)". That is false because there are not 3 conv layers. The paper says "shallow feature extraction by a convolutional layer, deep feature extraction by sequence of RSTB, then final conv". That's only 2 conv layers? Actually the final conv is also a convolution. So total conv layers number: 2? But they said "shallow feature extraction by a convolutional layer" (1). Then after RSTB maybe a final conv (1). So 2 conv layers. But they might also have some additional conv around reconstruction? The description says "shallow features are extracted by a convolutional layer; deep features are extracted by residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB) followed by a final convolutional layer. Finally, the image reconstruction layer is implemented with a sub-pixel convolutional layer." So final conv might be sub-pixel conv, maybe considered conv. So total conv layers: 3? 1 shallow + final conv + sub-pixel conv = 3? That might be considered 3 conv layers. But the statement says "contains 3 convolutional layers and a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks". Yes, that matches: there are 3 conv layers (shallow conv, final conv, sub-pixel conv). So maybe it's correct. But the statement says "SwinIR's structure contains 3 convolutional layers and a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB)". That is correct.

We need to see if that matches paper: The paper says: "SwinIR's structure contains three phases: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and image reconstruction. The shallow features are extracted by a convolutional layer whereas the deep features are extracted by a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB) followed by a final convolutional layer. Finally, the image reconstruction layer is implemented with a sub-pixel convolutional layer." So indeed it contains 3 conv layers: 1 shallow, 1 final conv, 1 sub-pixel conv. So the statement is correct.

D. "One of the reason that SDDPM can be used for denoising images obtained from the wild is it is able to map the noisy image to one of the noise levels it has been trained with and thereafter generate the denoised image". In the paper, they mention: "In the case of denoising real images, the exact amount of noise that is present in an image is unknown. It is also almost certain that the noisy images might have noise that does not exactly correspond to the αt values that we use for training our model. In such a scenario, the model should be able to map the noisy image to one of the noise levels it has been trained with and thereafter generate the denoised image. This makes the designed model robust and can be used for practical denoising applications." So statement D is correct.

Thus the incorrect statement is B. But we need to double-check: Are there any other statements that are incorrect? Let's verify A: The paper says: "Even for higher noise levels, the images denoised by SDDPM retain most of the structures that are present in the original images." So correct.

C: Reasonable as above.

Thus B is incorrect. The claim of exponential decrease is not supported. So answer B.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>\boxed{B}
